# Review of FDS Section 7.2 – CIP Sequence

## Summary

The draft lists the step names but does not define a sequence that can be built or tested. It has five main problems:

1. **No pass/fail criteria.** "Heated to temperature", "run until clean" and "to drain" cannot be programmed or verified at FAT/SAT.
2. **Cleaning is not verified at the return.** The skid has CT-501, TT-501 and FT-501, but the draft never uses them. Step timers should count only while the return temperature, concentration and supply flow are all in specification.
3. **There is no automatic fault handling.** "The operator should check the circuit" is not a control action. If P-502 stops while P-501 keeps running, solution will flood the silo or spill at the HTST.
4. **Circuit selection has no permissives.** "Any circuit selected on the HMI" can send hot caustic toward live product. There is nothing about product/CIP segregation, mix-proof valve proving, or the state of the silo or HTST.
5. **The two circuits are treated as identical.** S-1 (spray device, raw milk, mainly fat and protein soil) and HTST-1 (heated surfaces, milkstone and protein burn-on) need different recipes.

## Detailed Findings

| # | Draft text | Problem | Correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Open the rinse tank valve and run P-501 for 5 minutes to drain" | It is unclear whether "to drain" means the destination or the purpose. P-502 is not mentioned. There is no flow check, so 5 minutes may run with no flow at all. | Send the rinse once-through to drain with P-502 running. Count time only while FT-501 is at or above the minimum flow. |
| 2 | "Caustic tank is heated to temperature" | No setpoint is given. Tank temperature does not show that the circuit reached temperature. No concentration is given. | Define supply and return temperature setpoints and a caustic concentration. Measure them with TT-501 and CT-501. |
| 3 | "Circulate caustic for 20 minutes" | The timer starts too early. Water must first be pushed out, which is detected by conductivity at the return. No rule covers the timer if conditions drop out of specification. | Start the timer only when all conditions are in specification. Hold or reset the timer on deviation, as defined below. |
| 4 | Caustic step has no recovery | Caustic is either sent to drain, which wastes chemical, or recovered while still diluted, which weakens the tank. | Switch between drain and recovery on CT-501 thresholds at the start and end of the step. |
| 5 | "Intermediate rinse: 5 minutes to drain" | A fixed time does not prove the caustic is gone. Leftover caustic will neutralise the acid. | End the rinse on CT-501 falling below a setpoint, with a minimum time. |
| 6 | "Acid … 15 minutes at 65 C" | It does not say where 65 °C is measured. No concentration is given. One value is used for both circuits. | Use TT-501 at the return and set values per circuit recipe. Add an acid concentration via CT-501. |
| 7 | "Final rinse: Run until clean" | This cannot be tested. | End on CT-501 at or below the water-quality setpoint, held for a set time, with a minimum time. |
| 8 | No drain or purge between steps | Liquid left in the circuit dilutes the next chemical, and the silo can pool liquid. | Add a timed drain or scavenge after each step, with P-502 running. |
| 9 | No supervision of supply flow | Without enough velocity or spray coverage, the circuit is not cleaned. | Add a minimum flow per circuit on FT-501, with a low-flow alarm. |
| 10 | "If the return pump stops, the operator should check the circuit" | No automatic action is defined, so the circuit can flood or overflow. | Define an automatic response: stop P-501, close supply, hold the step, and alarm. |
| 11 | "Can be started on any circuit selected" | There is no interlock against product, no check of valve feedback, and nothing preventing both circuits being selected at once. | Add start permissives and run interlocks (section 7.2.2 below). |
| 12 | Mix-proof valves are not covered beyond routing | Valve seats and leakage chambers must be cleaned (seat lift). Valve position must be proven. | Add seat-lift pulsing and position-feedback checks. |
| 13 | No tank level or dry-run protection | P-501 can run dry. Chemical tanks can be emptied without warning. | Add low-level interlocks on each tank. |
| 14 | No sanitise step and no record keeping | Dairy regulatory practice (e.g. PMO in the US, or the site's QA plan) normally requires a recorded CIP and often a sanitise step before production. | Add an optional sanitise step and a CIP batch record. |
| 15 | No pause, abort or resume behaviour | Behaviour after a fault or power loss is undefined. | Define pause, abort and resume rules. |

## Proposed Rewrite

Values in **[brackets]** are typical starting points. They must be confirmed by the chemical supplier and site QA before the FDS is issued. Instruments marked *(TBC)* are not listed in the scope given and need confirming.

---

### 7.2 CIP Sequence

#### 7.2.1 General

- The skid cleans **one circuit at a time**: either Raw Milk Silo S-1 or Pasteurizer HTST-1.
- The operator selects the circuit on the HMI. Each circuit has its own recipe (section 7.2.5).
- All cleaning conditions are measured at the **return**:
  - temperature on TT-501;
  - concentration on CT-501.
- Supply flow is measured on FT-501.
- A step timer counts only while **all** of these "in-spec" conditions are true:
  - FT-501 ≥ the recipe minimum flow;
  - TT-501 ≥ the recipe minimum return temperature (chemical and hot-water steps);
  - CT-501 is inside the recipe concentration window (chemical steps);
  - P-502 is running, with running feedback confirmed.
- If any condition drops out during a chemical step:
  - the timer **holds**;
  - an alarm is raised.
- If the out-of-spec time exceeds **[60 s]**, the timer **resets to zero** for that step. The hold and reset times are configurable.

#### 7.2.2 Start Permissives

The sequence cannot start unless **all** of the following are true:

1. The selected circuit is not in production.
   - **S-1:** silo level ≤ [empty setpoint] *(level transmitter TBC)*. Outlet and inlet product valves are proven closed.
   - **HTST-1:** the HTST is in CIP mode, with the product feed stopped and the HTST controller handing over to CIP.
2. All mix-proof valves on the route have position feedback confirming the correct state. Every valve that separates the CIP route from product-containing lines is proven closed, and its leakage chamber is open to drain.
3. The other circuit is not selected and not running CIP.
4. The rinse, caustic and acid tanks are above their low-level start setpoints *(level switches/transmitters TBC)*.
5. The caustic and acid tanks are at their supply temperature setpoints, or the heater is enabled to bring them there before the chemical step.
6. P-501 and P-502 are healthy: no trips, and in Auto.
7. The operator confirms the selection on the HMI. For S-1, the operator also confirms that the manway is closed and the vent is clear.

#### 7.2.3 Sequence Steps

| Step | Description | Source → Destination | Start / Transition | Completion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Pre-rinse** | Rinse tank → circuit → drain (once-through) | P-501 and P-502 run. Timer counts while FT-501 ≥ min. | [5 min] in-spec time **and** CT-501 ≤ [rinse setpoint]. Then drain/scavenge for [60 s]. |
| 2 | **Caustic wash** | Caustic tank → circuit → drain, then → caustic tank (recirculation) | Return goes to drain until CT-501 ≥ [caustic arrival setpoint], then switches to caustic tank recovery. Timer starts when all in-spec conditions are met. | [Recipe time] in-spec. |
| 3 | **Caustic push-out / intermediate rinse** | Rinse tank → circuit → caustic tank, then → drain | Return goes to the caustic tank until CT-501 ≤ [recovery cut-off setpoint], then switches to drain. | [3 min] min **and** CT-501 ≤ [rinse setpoint] for [30 s]. Then drain/scavenge. |
| 4 | **Acid wash** | Acid tank → circuit → drain, then → acid tank | Same logic as step 2, using acid setpoints. | [Recipe time] in-spec. |
| 5 | **Acid push-out / final rinse** | Rinse tank (potable water) → circuit → acid tank, then → drain | Same logic as step 3. | [3 min] min **and** CT-501 ≤ [final rinse setpoint, e.g. potable water conductivity + margin] for [60 s]. Then drain/scavenge. |
| 6 | **Sanitise** (optional, selected in recipe or required before production) | [Hot water ≥ 85 °C return / sanitiser dosing – TBC] | Recipe-defined | Recipe-defined |
| 7 | **End** | — | Valves go to the safe state. Pumps stop. The circuit is flagged "Clean" with a timestamp. | — |

- **Mix-proof valve seat cleaning.** During steps 1 to 5, each mix-proof valve on the route performs upper and lower seat lifts. They run at [every 2 min], for [3 s] each, staggered so supply flow does not fall below the minimum. The seat lifts must be complete before a step can finish.
- **Drain between phases.** Each drain or scavenge period runs P-502 with P-501 stopped. This prevents liquid carryover and stops liquid pooling in the silo.

#### 7.2.4 Alarms and Fault Actions

| Condition | Automatic action | Operator action |
|---|---|---|
| P-502 fails or stops (no running feedback), or return flow is lost *(return flow / silo level TBC)* | **Immediately** stop P-501. Close the supply valve. Hold the step timer. Raise a high-priority alarm. For S-1, monitor silo level. | Investigate, then acknowledge and resume. The step timer follows the reset rule in 7.2.1. |
| P-501 fails, or FT-501 < min flow for [10 s] | Hold the timer and alarm. If the condition persists for [60 s], stop P-502 after a [scavenge time], then pause the sequence. | Investigate, then resume. |
| TT-501 < min during a chemical or hot step | Hold the timer and alarm. Reset the timer per 7.2.1. | — |
| CT-501 outside the window during a chemical step | Hold the timer and alarm. Reset the timer per 7.2.1. | Check the tank strength and dosing. |
| Valve position feedback mismatch | Stop P-501. Hold the timer. Alarm. If the valve is a segregating valve, **abort** the sequence. | Investigate. |
| Tank low level | Alarm, stop P-501, pause. | Replenish the tank. |
| Tank low-low level | Trip P-501 to protect against dry running. | — |
| Production start requested on a circuit under CIP | Block the request. | — |
| Power loss or PLC restart | The sequence restarts in **Paused**. The circuit status is set to "Not Clean". | Choose to resume the current step from zero or abort. |

#### 7.2.5 Recipe Parameters (per circuit)

| Parameter | S-1 Raw Milk Silo | HTST-1 Pasteurizer |
|---|---|---|
| Min supply flow (FT-501) | [Per spray device rating, m³/h] | [≥ 1.5 m/s in the largest line, m³/h] |
| Caustic return temperature (TT-501) | [≥ 70 °C] | [≥ 75–80 °C] |
| Caustic concentration | [0.5–1.0 % NaOH, as CT-501 setpoint] | [1.0–2.0 % NaOH] |
| Caustic in-spec time | [10–15 min] | [30–45 min] |
| Acid return temperature | [≥ 60 °C, or ambient per supplier] | [≥ 65–70 °C] |
| Acid concentration | [0.5–1.0 %] | [0.8–1.5 %] |
| Acid in-spec time | [10 min] | [15–20 min] |
| Final rinse conductivity setpoint | [µS/cm] | [µS/cm] |
| Sanitise step | [Optional] | [Required before production – TBC with QA] |

Note: CT-501 setpoints in mS/cm are temperature-compensated. The chemical supplier must supply conductivity-versus-concentration curves for each chemical.

#### 7.2.6 Operator Commands

- **Start** – only when all permissives are met.
- **Pause** – holds the step timer and stops P-501. P-502 scavenges and then stops.
- **Resume** – restarts from the current step. The timer follows the reset rule in 7.2.1.
- **Abort** – drains and scavenges, then moves to the safe state. The circuit is set to "Not Clean".
- **Advance step** – not available to operators. Available only with supervisor access, and logged.

#### 7.2.7 Records

For each CIP run, the system stores a batch record containing:

- circuit, recipe, operator and start/end timestamps;
- every step's start/end time and in-spec time;
- continuous trends of FT-501, TT-501 and CT-501;
- all alarms and operator actions.

The run result is **Pass** only if every step finished with its in-spec time met. The "Clean" status expires after **[72 h, TBC with QA]**, after which the circuit is "Not Clean".

---

## Open Items to Resolve Before Issue

1. Chemical concentrations, temperatures and times, confirmed with the chemical supplier and site QA.
2. Instruments not listed in scope:
   - tank level instruments;
   - silo level;
   - return flow or return-tank level for detecting P-502 loss;
   - steam/heater control for the chemical tanks.
3. HTST-1 CIP-mode handshake:
   - flow diversion valve cycling during CIP;
   - timing pump operation;
   - who controls the heating section.
4. Whether segregation needs to meet a specific regulation (e.g. PMO Appendix H in the US), which would make the mix-proof valve leak detection and segregation requirements formal.
5. Whether rinse water is reused: recovering final rinse water to the rinse tank for the next pre-rinse.
